Direct answer | This page's Gas Plant Operators corresponds to US SOC 51-8092.00, and the work can be divided into several categories: equipment monitoring and inspection — monitor equipment operation, observe temperature and liquid level and flow meters, and perform periodic unit inspections to ensure compressors and scrubbers and evaporators and refrigeration equipment and valves and instruments operate as expected; gas distribution and processing — use panels and control boards and semiautomatic equipment to distribute or process gas for utility companies and industrial customers, and control equipment to regulate the flow and pressure of gas sent to boilers and furnaces and related steam or heating equipment; compression and liquefaction and pressure regulation — control compressors and scrubbers and evaporators and refrigeration equipment to liquefy or compress or regasify natural gas, and adjust temperature and pressure and vacuum and liquid level and flow to keep the process within the required range; records and testing and collaboration — record, review and summarize operating records and test results and meter readings, test the purity and water content of gas and chemicals and air during the process to find quality problems or leaks, cooperate with other operators to solve unit problems and contact maintenance when needed. The four categories cycle in sequence: shift inspection and reading gauges — distribution and processing and pressure regulation — sampling and testing and recording — anomaly judgment and adjustment — handling and reporting per the real contingency plan. This page does not conflate this occupation with the adjacent compressor station operators or refinery operators or boiler operators or chemical plant operators.

There are also supplemental tasks including controlling fractionation columns and compressors and purification columns and heat exchangers to extract nitrogen and oxygen from air (80), calculating gas mixture ratios (69), operating construction equipment (60) and changing charts on recording instruments (57). The most important work activities are identifying objects and actions and events (84) and monitoring processes and materials or surroundings (84), followed by getting information (83) and making decisions and solving problems (83) and evaluating information to comply with standards (78) and inspecting equipment and structures or materials (77) and documenting and recording information (76).

entries.answer: This page's Gas Plant Operators corresponds to US SOC 51-8092.00: distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines. The core work includes monitoring equipment operation and observing temperature and liquid level and flow meters and performing periodic unit inspections; using panels and control boards and semiautomatic equipment to distribute or process gas; controlling compressors and scrubbers and evaporators and refrigeration equipment to liquefy or compress or regasify natural gas; controlling equipment to regulate the flow and pressure of gas sent to boilers and furnaces and related steam or heating equipment; recording, reviewing and summarizing operating records and test results and meter readings; determining the causes of abnormal pressure fluctuations and proposing and executing corrective measures; adjusting temperature and pressure and vacuum and liquid level and flow; cooperating with other operators to solve unit problems; and testing the purity and water content of gas and chemicals and air during the process to find quality problems or leaks. Common employers include utilities and pipeline transportation and natural gas liquefaction and purification and industrial gas supply organizations; what is described here is the US occupational classification basis.

entries.answer: The core difference lies in the object and the output: this occupation takes natural gas units and compressors and scrubbers and evaporators and refrigeration equipment and pressure regulation processes as its object, and its output is stable, verifiable gas distribution and processing and pressure regulation operation and parameter and test records; gas compressor and gas pumping station operators (53-7071.00) take pipeline compressor stations and pumping stations and pipeline pressure as their object; chemical plant and system operators (51-8091.00) produce chemical reaction and separation systems and product specifications; stationary engineers and boiler operators (51-8021.00) produce boilers and steam and heating equipment; petroleum pump system operators and refinery gaugers (51-8093.00) produce refinery units and product pumping and metering; control and valve installers and repairers (non-mechanical category, 49-9012.00) produce the installation, calibration and repair of control and valve devices. The objects and outputs all differ, and equipment adjustment and parameter setting and safety isolation and work permit authority cannot be carried over across positions.

subject.summary: Gas Plant Operators corresponds to US O*NET/SOC 51-8092.00 Gas Plant Operators: distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines. Monitor equipment operation and observe temperature and liquid level and flow meters and perform periodic unit inspections; use panels and control boards and semiautomatic equipment to distribute or process gas; control compressors and scrubbers and evaporators and refrigeration equipment to liquefy or compress or regasify natural gas; control equipment to regulate the flow and pressure of gas sent to boilers and furnaces and related steam or heating equipment; record, review and summarize operating records and test results and meter readings; determine the causes of abnormal pressure fluctuations and propose and execute corrective measures; adjust temperature and pressure and vacuum and liquid level and flow; cooperate with other operators to solve unit problems; test the purity and water content of gas and chemicals and air during the process to find quality problems or leaks. Official scope text: Distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines.
